findings.title: Migration crashes when legacy embed_category is missing or blank
findings.body: The migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` without checking for an empty result. `embed_category` is optional and often blank or unset; in that case the INNER JOIN query returns zero rows, `[0]` is nil, and the migration raises `NoMethodError`, blocking deployment. Use a safe fetch such as `first`/`try` before indexing.

findings.title: Legacy embeddable hosts are copied without normalization
findings.body: The migration inserts legacy `embeddable_hosts` values verbatim. The old matcher accepted entries with `http://`, `https://`, or trailing paths, while the new `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares the incoming URL's `URI#host` to the stored host string exactly. Existing site settings that contained scheme/path forms will stop matching after migration, breaking embedding for those hosts.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on nil host
findings.body: `before_validation` calls `sub!` directly on `self.host`. When `host` is nil or blank, possible via the admin create/update API, `nil.sub!` raises `NoMethodError`, returning a 500 instead of a normal validation failure. Guard the callback with `self.host.present?` or coerce with `self.host = self.host.to_s.sub(...)`.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint on host
findings.body: There is no unique validation or index on `host`. The admin API/UI can create multiple `EmbeddableHost` rows for the same host with different categories, while `record_for_host` returns the first one. Imported topics then use whichever row is returned first, making the host-to-category mapping ambiguous and nondeterministic.

findings.title: Missing record in update/destroy becomes fatal
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without handling nil. A request with a deleted or unknown id passes nil to `save_host` or calls `destroy` on nil, causing a 500 instead of a 404 or JSON error response.

findings.title: Host entries with ports cannot match
findings.body: The format validation allows a port such as `example.com:8080`, but `record_for_host` compares `URI(host).host`, which drops the port, against the stored host string. A stored host with a port can never match an incoming referer, so such entries appear valid in admin but silently deny embeds. Either strip ports on save and adjust lookup, or disallow them.

findings.title: Fabricator definitions are in the wrong files
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now contains `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the category fabricators. Fabrication may load them regardless, but the file names no longer describe their contents and future maintenance by filename will be misleading.

findings.title: /fruits/:id fixture ignores the requested id
findings.body: The pretender route always returns `fruits[0]` regardless of `:id`. The updated store test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` but still gets fruit 1; the plural `color_ids` assertions happen to pass because fruit 1 also has two colors. This means the test does not actually exercise lookup of a different record and could mask regressions.
